168	
169	**This table selects a MODE; it does not discover units.** No Recognition cell
170	mints a unit. For the five rows that name a **compilation** universe —
171	`ts-tsconfig`, `js-allowjs`, `js-synthesized`, `rust-cargo` and
172	`rust-cargo-prepared` — the cell is read **after** §1.4 U-1 has yielded a unit of
173	that language family, because those modes describe a program and a program needs
174	one. **`syntax-only` carries no such prerequisite and must not be read as if it
175	did:** it is the compiler-free path, it has no compilation unit at all (§1.2's
176	third-universe paragraph and §6.3's grammar dialect branch both depend on that),
177	and it is exactly what serves a repository in which U-1 yields **no** TS or Rust
178	unit. A file reached that way is `syntax-only` membership with `unitOrdinal: null`
179	under U-4, not a member of an invented unit. U-1 is the specific model — the closed `WorkspaceUnitV2` record,
180	the exactly-once `FileMembershipRowV1` law and the marker precedence
181	`tsconfig.json` > `jsconfig.json` > `package.json` — and a `tsjs` unit exists only
182	where a directory holds one of those three markers. So a directory of bare `.js`
183	files with no marker is **not** a unit: under U-4 each such file is
184	`syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language`, never a program member,
185	and no `js-synthesized` program is minted for them. An
186	earlier wording of the `js-synthesized` row read as an independent recognition
187	test ("`package.json` present **or** any `.js` file under the unit"), and an
188	implementer taking it alone would have minted units for bare-`.js` directories,
189	changing unit membership and therefore the Plan. The disjunct was never reachable
190	under U-1 — with no `tsconfig.json`, no `jsconfig.json` and no `package.json`
191	there is no unit for a `.js` file to be "under" — and the cell now says what it
192	always meant: within a U-1 unit whose marker is `package.json`, `.js` files are
193	program roots.
194	
195	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
196	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
197	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
198	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
199	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
200	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
201	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
202	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
203	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
204	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
205	
206	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
207	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
208	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
209	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
210	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
211	
212	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
213	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
214	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
215	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
216	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
217	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
218	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
219	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
220	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
221	  semantics the mode never computes.
222	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
223	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
224	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
225	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
226	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
227	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
228	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
229	  as a resolution claim.
230	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
231	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
232	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
233	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
234	  suffix must map to one grammar
235	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
236	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
237	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
238	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
239	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
240	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
241	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
242	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
243	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
244	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
245	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
246	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
247	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
248	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
249	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
250	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
251	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
252	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
253	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
254	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
255	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
256	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
257	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
258	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
259	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
260	
261	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
262	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
263	
264	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
265	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
266	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
267	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
268	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
269	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
270	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
271	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
272	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
273	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
274	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
275	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
276	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
277	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
278	
279	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
280	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
281	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
282	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
283	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
284	languages instead of ignoring four.
285	
286	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
287	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
288	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
289	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
290	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
291	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
292	
293	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
294	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
295	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
296	
297	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
298	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
299	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
300	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
301	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
302	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
303	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
304	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
305	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
306	whether facts happen to exist:
307	
308	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
309	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
310	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
311	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
312	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
313	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
314	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
315	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
316	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
317	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
318	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
319	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
320	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
321	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
322	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
323	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
324	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
325	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
326	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
327	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
328	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
329	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
330	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
331	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
332	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
333	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
334	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
335	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
336	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
337	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
338	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
339	  exactly as the matrix already says.
340	
341	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
342	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
343	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
344	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
345	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
346	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
347	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
348	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
349	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
350	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
351	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
352	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
353	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
354	
355	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
356	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
357	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
358	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
359	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
360	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
361	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
362	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
363	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
364	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
365	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
366	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
367	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
368	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
369	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
370	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
371	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
372	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
373	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
374	cross-universe defect.
375	
376	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
377	**not** contain is owed nothing —
378	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
379	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
380	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
381	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
382	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
383	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
384	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
385	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
386	row, and never inferred. This is the specific rule that identity §3's "partition
387	the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions" defers to: the **disjointness**
388	half is general, applies within the full owning
389	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` tuple, and is
390	decided at retained Run closure against the registry's own
391	`coveragePartitionLaw`; the **omission** half is discharged only where this
392	registry carries a `coverageTotality` row. For the nine `symbol`-kind relations it
393	carries none, and the reason is the trust boundary stated below — symbol-to-file
394	attribution is not re-derivable from the retained Run — so no fact-per-symbol
395	obligation exists there. Evaluator3 separately requires the selected symbol
396	inventory and accounts for required work over its independently retained census
397	(identity §4). A symbol may have no call/reference fact, while a whole expected
398	inventory or work partition cannot silently disappear. Disjointness still applies, because it
399	asks a different question: not what was examined, but whether one interpretation
400	claimed a subject twice.
401	
402	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
403	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
404	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
405	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
406	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
407	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
408	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
409	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
410	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
411	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
412	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
413	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
414	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
415	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
416	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
417	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
418	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
419	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
420	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
421	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
422	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
423	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
424	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
425	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
426	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
427	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
428	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
429	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
430	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
431	
432	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
433	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
434	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
435	
436	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
437	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
438	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
439	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
440	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
441	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
442	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
443	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
444	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
445	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
446	
447	This particular guard — the one decided by the **selected grammar rows** — is
448	**syntax-universe specific**. Every *semantic* capability of the TypeScript and
449	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
450	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
451	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
452	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
453	compiler-ownership obligation.
454	
455	It is **not** the only scope-capability guard, and an earlier revision of this
456	paragraph read as if it were. A separate and weaker law, stated in §10 and
457	published as
458	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/scopeCapabilityLaw`, applies
459	to **any** universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table — TypeScript and
460	the syntax universe both — and asks only whether a scoped path's own suffix
461	selects a variant in the table that universe published. For the syntax universe
462	that condition is strictly weaker than the grammar law above and is implied by
463	it, because the capability registry's `data-document` class law already states
464	that **no suffix of a data grammar appears in the syntax dialect table**. For
465	TypeScript it is the *only* such law, and it is what a `clones` scope over
466	`package.json` is now answered by. Which guard reaches a given scope first,
467	however, is decided by what each boundary can see, not by which law is stronger.
468	The suffix law needs nothing but the scope's own paths, so the native Coverage
469	producer boundary already applies it to the one case it can judge from a single
470	record — a `source-path` relation carrying a body-identity join, which is
471	`clones` — whenever the caller hands it the owning universe's dialect, as Run
472	closure does. Closure runs that producer admission **before** any of its own
473	prerequisites, so a false claim of complete Coverage for a `clones` scope over
474	a path no dialect table lists is refused there, as a producer-admission failure
475	naming the source variant, before the grammar guard. The grammar law is neither weakened nor reordered: among
476	closure's own prerequisites it is still applied ahead of the suffix backstop,
477	and it remains the sole owner, under its own refusal names, of everything a
478	suffix table cannot see — the `symbol` relations, the other syntax relations,
479	and the selection case where a path's suffix *is* in the table but no selected
480	grammar row owns it. An honestly disclosed unsupported scope still carries
481	`coverage: unknown` and the published `language-tier-unsupported` /
482	`capability-missing` pair. A false claim of complete Coverage is rejected; its
483	internal first-refusal name depends on which admission boundary detects it.
484	
485	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
486	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
487	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
488	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
489	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
490	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
491	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
492	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
493	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
494	supported one.
495	
496	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
497	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
498	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
499	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
500	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating

501	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
502	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
503	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
504	scope therefore remains admissible.
505	
506	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
507	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
508	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
509	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
510	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
511	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
512	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
513	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
514	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
515	
516	**JavaScript option and universe-flag derivation.** `allowJs` and `checkJs`
517	in the retained context are effective, materialized booleans from the selected
518	compiler's resolved configuration, including the retained configuration graph.
519	For the selected option projection, every node of that graph whose `kind` is
520	`jsconfig` (the exact basename law of `TypeScriptConfigGraphV1`) supplies
521	`allowJs=true` as if written in that node, unless the node itself writes
522	`allowJs`. Inheritance then applies over the graph: a node's own options,
523	including that supplied value, take precedence over the bases it extends, and
524	later `extends` entries over earlier ones. After inheritance an `allowJs` value
525	wins, including `false`; otherwise `allowJs` derives from the effective
526	`checkJs`, whose omitted default is `false`. So a `jsconfig.json` entry extending
527	a base that writes `allowJs: false` is effective `allowJs=true` unless the entry
528	writes `allowJs` itself, and a `tsconfig.json` entry extending a base named
529	`jsconfig.json` inherits `true`. The pre-Plan marker observation
530	named `allowJs` also means this effective value, never mere presence of the raw
531	configuration property. `js-allowjs` versus `ts-tsconfig` selection uses that
532	value. The synthesized profile keeps its separately specified `true`/`false`
533	values. This derivation agrees with the version-pinned [TypeScript compiler
534	computed option](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/blob/v5.6.3/src/compiler/utilities.ts#L8919);
535	that source is supporting evidence, not a required product toolchain version.
536	
537	The two universe flags have exact, distinct laws:
538	- `jsAdmittedToProgram = configProjection.honoredOptions.allowJs AND
539	  (len(universe.jsRootFiles) > 0)`.
540	- `jsDiagnosticsEnabled = configProjection.honoredOptions.checkJs`.
541	
542	`jsRootFiles` is the admitted compiler root-file set already joined to the
543	universe; the first flag is about those JS roots, not a claim that every possible
544	transitive JavaScript module was found. Enabling `allowJs` with no JS roots does
545	not make the first flag true. Diagnostic enablement does not require a nonempty
546	JS-root set and does not attest that any diagnostic ran or that compilation
547	succeeded. An explicit `allowJs=false` with `checkJs=true` retains those effective
548	option values; they do not assert that the compiler accepts that configuration.
549	The option projection must not rewrite explicit `false` to `true` to suppress
550	a configuration diagnostic. **This law introduces no compiler-option diagnostic
551	refusal.** A compiler option diagnostic, including TypeScript diagnostic 5052 for
552	`allowJs=false` with `checkJs=true`, neither refuses admission nor creates a
553	deficiency, native cause or diagnostic carrier under this law, and this contract
554	names no owner that routes such a diagnostic: a universe with those effective
555	values is admitted with them, and whether the compiler accepted the configuration
556	is not recorded by these flags (a stated limit, not a delegation). The law changes
557	no effective option value, typed-context field or schema admission beyond the
558	derivation above.
559	The corresponding native context/universe field disagreement refuses through
560	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
561	
562	These options and flags are universe keys. `checkJs` controls diagnostics, and
563	can affect membership through the omitted-`allowJs` default above; it does not
564	supply resolution evidence. Neither flag grants a capability or establishes
565	that resolution was attempted or complete. Resolution completeness is asserted
566	only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3); `resolutionCompletenessImplied` remains `false`.
567	
568	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
569	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
570	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
571	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

596	Limitations (closed ids; each is disclosed in Coverage, never hidden):

598	- **L-JS1** synthesized options: `paths`/`baseUrl`/`rootDirs`/custom `types` are unknown; a specifier resolvable only through them is `unresolved-module-specifier`.
599	- **L-JS2** dynamic forms: computed member access, non-literal `require`/`import()`, indirect `eval`, reflective access and `any`-typed calls produce unresolved edges; resolution completeness for universal negatives is then `incomplete` (§4).

602	- **L-RS2** dynamic dispatch and generics: `dyn Trait` calls resolve to the trait method declaration and are recorded as `trait-object-dynamic-dispatch` unresolved edges; generic bound calls as `generic-bound-dispatch`. Both count against resolution completeness for universal negatives.

Declarative `macro_rules!` expansion is compiler-native and fully supported.

608	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
609	
610	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
611	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
612	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
613	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
614	share a root.
615	
616	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
617	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
618	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
619	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
620	
621	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
622	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
623	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
624	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.
625	
626	- **U-0 (internal root representation, normative)** `rootPath` and every
627	  `memberPackageRoots[]` entry are the **internal** relative directory form and nothing
628	  else. `rootPath` is the empty string `` for the project root, or a canonical relative
629	  directory (`#/$defs/InternalUnitRootV1`); a member package root is always a NON-EMPTY
630	  canonical relative directory (`#/$defs/CanonicalRelativeDirV1`), because a member is
631	  always strictly inside its workspace root. A canonical relative directory is one or more
632	  `/`-joined non-empty segments with no leading or trailing `/`, no empty segment, no `.`
633	  or `..` segment, no NUL and no backslash. `CanonicalPath` is deliberately NOT this
634	  grammar: it admits a trailing `/` and an interior empty segment (`a//b`), neither of
635	  which is canonical for a directory used as a membership prefix.
636	  `.` is the **external** sentinel only, on both edges: Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots`
637	  and CLI `--workspace-root` inbound (`normalize_explicit_root`, `.` -> ``), and the
638	  outward `workspaceRoot` of the shared scope record and of enumeration cells
639	  (`spell_root`, `` -> `.`). A retained `WorkspaceUnitV2` is **never** normalized after
640	  retention, because `rootPath` is consumed as an exact string prefix by U-3 membership, by
641	  relative-path slicing and by the deepest-unit `len(rootPath)` ranking.
642	  A unit whose root is not in internal form is refused **before** membership, slicing or
643	  enumeration binding reads it (`admit_unit_roots`; internal decision key
644	  `NATIVE_UNIT_ROOT_REPRESENTATION`, and `ENUMERATION_MEMBERSHIP_UNIT_ROOT` when the same
645	  decision is reached through enumeration admission). This is an INTERNAL host-invariant
646	  decision and adds no public detail code; a malformed EXTERNAL root keeps its existing
647	  typed public refusal `native.explicit-root-grammar` (CONFIG.INVALID). Deciding it first
648	  is the whole point: `.` makes every U-3 prefix test false, so the unit would silently own
649	  no file and the result would be an empty but schema-valid analysis, and the enumeration
650	  join would otherwise surface the same wrong root as `ENUMERATION_BINDING_PROGRAM_ENTRY`,
651	  attributing it to a different field.
652	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
653	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
654	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
655	  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
656	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`).
657	  Both configuration markers use the effective `allowJs` value from §1.2: false selects
658	  `ts-tsconfig`, true selects `js-allowjs`; an omitted value defaults to false for a
659	  `tsconfig.json` entry and true for a `jsconfig.json` entry. The
660	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
661	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
662	  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
663	- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
664	  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
665	  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
666	  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
667	  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
668	  selection, never loss of Cargo workspace semantics (post-reset v2 A-3/P22):**
669	  naming a Cargo workspace root explicitly yields exactly the automatic result
670	  for that unit (members folded, member `target` output pruned, a member's
671	  `src/target` still source); naming a member package alone selects that package
672	  as its own `cargo-package` unit, and files of the unselected root or siblings
673	  are honest `no-program-unit-for-language` rows, neither claimed nor
674	  over-ignored (`units-explicit-cargo-workspace-root-keeps-member-folding-and-member-target-pruning`).
675	- **U-3 (deterministic membership within a language)** A file's family is fixed
676	  by extension (`.rs` → `rust`; `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` → `tsjs`).
677	  It belongs to the **deepest unit of its own family** whose root prefixes its
678	  path. Units of another family never claim it. Nested monorepo packages
679	  (`packages/web/tsconfig.json` under a root `tsconfig.json`) are therefore
680	  distinct `tsjs` units and the deeper one wins for its subtree
681	  (`units-nested-monorepo-deepest-within-language-and-workspace-folding`).
682	- **U-4 (no source erasure; honest unsupported files)** Every snapshot inventory
683	  file appears in exactly one `FileMembershipRowV1`: `program-member`;
684	  `syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language` (a `.rs` file with no
685	  enclosing Rust unit: semantic rungs `unknown`, cause `no-program-unit`),
686	  `grammar-only` (bundled grammar, no program) or `host-ignore-convention`
687	  (the file lies inside a pruned tree of the shared rule below); or
688	  `unsupported-file` with reason `no-bundled-grammar`, listed in
689	  `unsupportedFiles`. `erasedFiles` is a schema-constant empty array
690	  (`maxItems 0`) and the model refuses a membership that does not cover the
691	  inventory exactly once.
692	- **U-4a (one shared discovery rule; post-reset MUST-3)** The host ignore

copy and module-name prefixes rebound to source40. No expectation is edited; the port is recorded in

import hashlib, json
from pathlib import Path

OLD = Path('/private/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/claude-independent-design.v39/probes')
NEW = Path('/private/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/claude-independent-design.v40/probes')

    src = (OLD / name).read_bytes()
    text = src.decode('utf-8')
    out = (text.replace('claude-independent-design.v39', 'claude-independent-design.v40')
               .replace('work/source39-pkg', 'work/source40-pkg')
               .replace("'p39_", "'p40_").replace('"p39_', '"p40_'))

1419	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
1420	
1421	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
1422	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
1423	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
1424	own language and refuses the other.
1425	
1426	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
1427	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
1428	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
1429	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
1430	
1431	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
1432	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
1433	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
1434	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
1435	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
1436	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
1437	descriptor and tree.
1438	
1439	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
1440	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
1441	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
1442	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
1443	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
1444	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
1445	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
1446	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
1447	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
1448	
1449	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
1450	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
1451	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).

1453	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
1454	
1455	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
1456	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
1457	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
1458	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.
1459	
1460	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
1461	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
1462	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.
1463	
1464	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
1465	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
1466	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
1467	
1468	| Field | Produced from |
1469	|---|---|
1470	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
1471	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
1472	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
1473	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A missing row refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<name>`, because an alternate partial declaration inventory for the same retained library is not the required complete record. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
1474	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` **names** the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must map to a retained component under the published name-to-component join below. These are `lib` names (`es2022`), never declaration-file names |
1475	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1476	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1477	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
1478	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
1479	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
1480	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
1481	
1482	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1483	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1484	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1485	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1486	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1487	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1488	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1489	
1490	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1491	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1492	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1493	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1494	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1495	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1496	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1497	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1498	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1499	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1500	divergence, not implementation freedom.

1501	
1502	| Rule | Statement |
1503	|---|---|
1504	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1505	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1506	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1507	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1508	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1509	
1510	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1511	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1512	
1513	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1514	|---|---|---|---|
1515	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1516	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1517	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1518	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1519	
1520	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1521	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1522	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1523	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1524	
1525	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1526	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1527	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1528	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1529	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1530	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1531	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1532	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1533	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1534	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1535	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1536	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1537	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1538	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1539	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1540	
1541	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1542	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1543	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1544	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1545	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1546	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1547	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1548	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1549	which two paths share a basename refuses
1550	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1551	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1552	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1553	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1554	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1555	
1556	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1557	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1558	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1559	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1560	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1561	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1562	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1563	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1564	
1565	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1566	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1567	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1568	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1569	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1570	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1571	
1572	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1573	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1574	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1575	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1576	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1577	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1578	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1579	the admitted id refuse
1580	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1581	
1582	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1583	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1584	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1585	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1586	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1587	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1588	
1589	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1590	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1591	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1592	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1593	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1594	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1595	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1596	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
1597	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1598	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
1599	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
1600	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
1601	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
1602	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
1603	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
1604	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public

1635	## 3. Sealed dependency inputs (AR-07)
1636	
1637	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1638	
1639	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1640	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1641	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1642	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1643	
1644	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1645	
1646	| Field | Rule |
1647	|---|---|
1648	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1649	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1650	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1651	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1652	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1653	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1654	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1655	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1656	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1657	
1658	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1659	
1660	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1661	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1662	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1663	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1664	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1665	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1666	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1667	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1668	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1669	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1670	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1671	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1672	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1673	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1674	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1675	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1676	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1677	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1678	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1679	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1680	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1681	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1682	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1683	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1684	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1685	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1686	  syntax analysis.
1687	
1688	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1689	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1690	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1691	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

1694	
1695	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1696	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses

1703	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1704	
1705	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1706	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1707	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1708	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1709	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1710	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1711	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
1712	
1713	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1714	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1715	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
1716	
1717	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
1718	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
1719	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
1720	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
1721	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
1722	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.
1723	- **CC-3** The constructed environment contains no `PATH`, `CARGO_*`, `RUSTFLAGS`,
1724	  `RUSTC*`, `RUSTDOC*`, `RUSTUP_*`, `CC`/`CXX`/`LD`/`AR`/`TARGET_*` variables;
1725	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
1726	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
1727	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
1728	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
1729	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
1730	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.
1731	
1732	Projected (honored) keys: `build.target`, `build.rustflags`,
1733	`target.<triple>.rustflags` (both through the flag allowlist below),
1734	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,
1735	`resolver`, and `[patch]` in `Cargo.toml`. Stripped and recorded: `alias`,
1736	`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`,
1737	`build.rustdoc`, `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.incremental`,
1738	`build.dep-info-basedir`, `cargo-new`, `credential-alias`, `doc`, `env`,

1746	file** the adapter materializes under CC-5 — a raw artifact digest of a file.
1747	`rust-v2.configProjectionSha256` (§2.1) is the 64-hex suffix of
1748	`H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the whole

1792	### 3.6 `PreparedOutputSetV3`: inert rows only (feedback 4, R2)
1793	
1794	Domain `native.prepared-output-set.v3` (revised in place; v3 was never accepted).
1795	`{schemaVersion:3, preparation: {kind: authorized-execution|imported-descriptor,
1796	authorizationId|null, importId|null, toolchain, dependencySourceSetId, cfgSetId,
1797	producer}, rows: [PreparedOutputRowV3…]}`.
1798	
1799	`PreparedOutputRowV3`: `{kind, ownerKey, configuration, site|null, generated|null,
1800	inputBinding: {ownerFileManifestSha256, dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest,
1801	cfgSetId}, blob: {sha256, byteLength, mediaType}, status: ok|failed,
1802	failureDetail|null}`.
1803	
1804	- **PO-0 (inert by kind and consumption channel; a media type is a label, never a
1805	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:
1806	  `build-script-directives` (`text/x-cargo-directives`: the captured `cargo:`
1807	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),
1808	  `macro-expansion` (`text/x-rust-expansion`: the fully expanded token text for one
1809	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
1810	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
1811	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file
1812	  a build script wrote under `OUT_DIR`). Row kinds `proc-macro-dylib` and
1813	  `build-script-binary` are refused **regardless of the media type they claim**
1814	  (a dylib relabelled `text/x-rust-expansion` is still a dylib row), and a media
1815	  type outside the kind's set is refused; either is
1816	  `native.prepared-output-not-inert` (exit 2), from an import *and* from the
1817	  in-host step alike (`generated-file-media-type-is-not-trust-proof-kind-decides`).
1818	  **No prepared artifact is ever loaded, linked or executed by the semantic
1819	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
1820	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
1821	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).
1822	- **PO-4 (generated-file input closure and the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`)**
1823	  The worker resolves `env!("OUT_DIR")` for owner *O* to the read-only virtual
1824	  path `.opensip/out/v1/<ownerKey>/` in its sealed VFS. A site
1825	  `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"))` (likewise
1826	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to
1827	  `(ownerKey, logicalPath="generated.rs")` whose `inputBinding` equals the current
1828	  context, and consumes its bytes **only** as Rust source text, a string literal or
1829	  a byte literal respectively. A miss (no row, stale binding, failed owner) is a
1830	  typed unknown: `build-script-generated-unavailable` edge, cause
1831	  `generated-file-missing`; it is never a hard failure and never a fallback to a
1832	  host path (`generated-file-include-out-dir-resolves-inert`,
1833	  `generated-file-missing-is-typed-unknown-not-failure`). Strict bounds
1834	  (`GeneratedInputBoundsV1`): `logicalPath` is a strict relative path (no `/`
1835	  prefix, no `.`/`..` segment, no NUL or backslash, ≤ 1024 bytes; an escaping path
1836	  fails exact typed admission and the worker lookup independently refuses it with
1837	  cause `generated-file-out-of-bounds`), `maxGeneratedFilesPerOwner 4096`,
1838	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
1839	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to
1840	  archive members by exact `blobs[]` digest; an archive member outside the
1841	  wrapper's `blobs` is never read (`generated-file-path-escape-and-bounds-refused`).
1842	- **PO-1 (staleness)** A row is usable only if `inputBinding` equals the current
1843	  context (owner manifest, dependency set, toolchain digest, cfg set). A stale row
1844	  is refused before Plan construction (`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, detail
1845	  `native.stale-prepared-output`, listing the differing fields) when prepared mode
1846	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and
1847	  non-prepared fallback when prepared mode was defaulted. It never uses a stale blob.
1848	- **PO-2 (failed rows)** A `failed` build script is retained as a row so the same
1849	  inputs need not be re-run; the owner is analyzed non-prepared
1850	  (`build-script-generated-unavailable`).
1851	- **PO-3 (imported)** An imported set carries the same binding fields and
1852	  `provenanceAssurance: declared`; the host cannot verify that an external

1854	  Plan-bound and disclosed with the import identity and producer.
1855	
1856	Where do the expansions and generated files come from? From the **preparation
1857	step** (§5.3), which is the only place proc-macro dylibs are built and loaded and
1858	build scripts run, inside the authorized `repository-code` principal with live
1859	boundaries. The step captures the required generated **data** and discards every
1860	executable product; its output is the inert row set, and the worker consumes only

1865	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1866	
1867	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1868	
1869	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1870	
1871	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1872	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1873	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1874	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1875	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1876	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1877	
1878	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1879	
1880	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1881	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1882	
1883	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1884	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1885	
1886	```
1887	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1888	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1889	```
1890	
1891	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1892	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1893	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1894	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1895	
1896	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1897	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1898	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1899	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1900	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1901	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1902	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1903	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1904	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1905	
1906	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1907	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1908	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1909	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1910	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1911	against a value the provider never supplied.
1912	
1913	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1914	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1915	
1916	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1917	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1918	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1919	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1920	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1921	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1922	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1923	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1924	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1925	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1926	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1927	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1928	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1929	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1930	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1931	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1932	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1933	
1934	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1935	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1936	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1937	
1938	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1939	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1940	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1941	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1942	
1943	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1944	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1945	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1946	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1947	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1948	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1949	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.

2337	
2338	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
2339	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2340	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
2341	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
2342	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
2343	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
2344	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
2345	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
2346	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2347	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2348	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2349	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.
2350	
2351	**The two clauses have different scopes, and the second is deliberately the wider
2352	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2353	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2354	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only
2355	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2356	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2357	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2358	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2359	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It
2360	is not read as types-scoped, and reading it that way would be a *weakening* — it
2361	would permit a native `clones` or `references` provider to emit a fabricated
2362	percentage, which is exactly what §4.8 removed.
2363	
2364	That leaves `ViewEntryV3.confidenceMillionths`, whose domain is the full integer
2365	range 0…1000000 and which carries **no** `confidenceMethod`. The wider domain is
2366	deliberate and is what keeps §4.6 step 3 reachable: the floor comparison is the
2367	sufficiency evaluation's, it runs for **every** relation, and it must still decide
2368	correctly against an entry a conforming native provider would never have emitted —
2369	a defective or non-conforming provider, and the defensive fixture below. No
2370	*imported* route is offered as an example and none is implied: imported evidence
2371	is a separate plane that mints no `ViewEntryV3` at all (§7, workflows §4), so it
2372	could not supply one of these values, and inventing such a path to explain the

2374	`sufficiency-v2-confidence-floor-precedes-one-rung-existential-shortcut` is

322	## Retained input selection and complete replay
323	
324	`evaluator_input_model.v3.py` reconstructs the composition inputs using the native/schema/identity owner's admitted closure. It reads no claimed finding, witness value or verdict. Every selected Plan import is an evaluation input, including a wrapper whose scope has no matching subject; omission is structural. A non-null ImportObservation member must agree with the same claim in its canonical payload: runtime window/population, test selection, history range endpoints. Observation kind must equal wrapper kind, and members inapplicable to that kind are null. Null is undisclosed information; it is not a contrary positive assertion and is never filled with a fictional observation. The canonical payload remains the owner of its own declared selection/range/window.
325	
326	Each atom is evaluated against the complete admitted evaluation input selection, retaining availability and empty-population inputs as well as hits. `predicate-witness` has no `inputRefs` field. That complete selection is projected onto every atomic `predicateProofs[].inputRefs` as specified in §9; boolean nodes take the canonical union of immediate children. Atom-model consumed-ref subsets are not evaluator3 proof fields. Coverage deficiencies retain their original native cause and source universe. Inputs are immutable preimages; a retained native extraction assertion remains provider evidence, and replay does not rerun a compiler to establish extraction truth.
327	
328	`evaluator_replay_model.v3.py` first admits the retained owner graph, reconstructs inputs, invokes the actual atom scanner and composes complete outputs. It compares every recomputed proof field and every output object/blob preimage, then independently reconstructs semantic evidence, seal and Run. It compares full finding identities, message/parameter bytes, severity, citations, waivers and enumeration outcomes, not counts. The authoritative evidence view set equals selected view inputs; its coverage set is the union of those views' coverage plus explicit admitted coverage inputs. Additional retained unreachable objects do not become authoritative findings.
329	
330	The synthetic reference harness uses a temporary graph only to open the legacy owner closure, whose API is Run-based. Its provisional outputs are discarded as semantic answers: reconstruction uses only Plan, execution and retained inputs. The exported positive Run is newly composed and must pass complete replay. Real extraction and platform qualification remain separate required work.
331	
332	The public `identity-model.v3.close_run` boundary invokes complete replay. Storage preparation/restoration and cache admission against an authoritative Run inherit that stronger check. `open_run_closure` is an internal owner-admission primitive; calling it alone is not a claim that evaluator3 output is correct. Intermediate cache-key construction remains possible before a Run and grants no authority.
333	
334	Every explicit coverage input must also belong to a selected admitted view, so the owner's coverage producer-admission and unresolved-edge accounting have run for it. A coverage wrapper by itself is not a substitute for that native view admission. The normalized scanner receives exact import wrappers plus separately derived import-scope and current/consumable maps from owner admission; those are host projections, not caller-supplied result flags.
